response.text:
I can’t change your mail directly — you said no email tools are available, and I don’t have access to perform destructive actions. Before you (or I, if tools become available) remove those 37 messages I need two things from you:

1) Pick the action (archive or delete). Quick guidance:
   - Archive — safer. Removes messages from your inbox but keeps them in “All Mail” (recoverable).
   - Delete (Move to Trash) — more permanent. Messages stay in Trash ~30 days before permanent removal (unless you manually empty Trash). Use this only if you’re sure.

2) Confirm the exact target. You wrote “37 old recruiting messages.” Do you mean:
   - All messages returned by a search for recruiter/recruiting/job-opportunity keywords and older than X months?
   - Messages from specific senders (e.g., from particular recruiter domains)?
   - The exact 37 currently visible in your inbox (I can’t see them, so say “Yes — the 37 shown when I search for …”)?

If you want to do it yourself now, here are simple Gmail instructions (web and mobile):

Gmail web (desktop)
1. In the search box enter a search that finds those recruiting messages. Examples:
   - recruiter OR recruiting OR "job opportunity" older_than:6m
   - subject:(recruit OR recruiting) older_than:1y
   Adjust the time (older_than:6m / older_than:1y) until the result count is 37.
2. Verify the results show the 37 messages you mean.
3. Click the checkbox at top-left to select messages; then click the “Select all conversations that match this search” link that appears to include all results.
4. Click Archive (box with downward arrow) to archive, or the Trash/Delete icon to delete.
5. If you delete, you can permanently remove them immediately by going to Trash and clicking “Empty Trash now,” or wait ~30 days for automatic deletion.

Gmail mobile app
1. Use the search bar with similar keywords (e.g., recruiter OR recruiting).
2. Long-press one message to enter selection mode, tap others (or use “Select all” if available).
3. Tap Archive or Delete.

If you want, tell me:
- Which action to take (archive or delete), and
- Which search criteria to use (I can suggest a tighter query if you give an example sender or subject text).

Once you confirm (for example reply “Archive the 37 recruiting messages found with search: recruiter OR recruiting older_than:6m”), I’ll either (A) give a ready-to-copy exact search + step sequence for you, or (B) if tools become available later, perform the requested action after reconfirming. Which do you want?
